question.text: The Ottomans conquered this capital city of the Byzantine Empire in May 1453. Give its name as of 1453, not its ancient name or its modern name, which was adopted in 1923.
question.answerHtml: Constantinople (do not accept or prompt on “Byzantium” or “Istanbul”)
question.clue: A road called the mese (MEH-say) ran through this city, which may have lost forty percent of its population in a plague in 542 CE. A gigantic cannon designed by Orban sufficed to break through this city's 60-foot-tall Theodosian Walls.

swap.text: The Byzantine Empire had several rulers with this common name; the first of whom usurped the throne from Michael III and founded the Macedonian dynasty, and the second was known as the Bulgar-slayer for his complete conquest of Bulgaria.
swap.clue: In addition to naming the brother-in-law of Vladimir I of Kiev, this name belongs to a ruler who overthrew Michael III and had Ignatius installed over Photius as patriarch of Constantinople.

question.text: This Byzantine Emperor tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Mediterranean, and this husband of Theodora was targeted in the Nika Riots.
question.clue: Peter Barsymes collected taxes under this ruler, who is accused of killing a myriad myriad of myriads and of being a demon who can make his head disappear in the Secret History of Procopius .

swap.text: Constantinople was earlier sacked during this campaign, which led to the decline of the Byzantine Empire. Enrico Dandolo, the Doge of Venice, had earlier led this campaign.
swap.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

question.leadin: Name some things about the times when the use of religious images were opposed by both religious and Byzantine authority.
question.text: Name that time period during which depictions of religious figures was directly opposed by the leaders of the Eastern Church.
question.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

swap.text: This general of Justinian, who exiled Pope Silverius, reconquered much of the Western Roman Empire from the Vandals and Goths.
swap.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

question.leadin: Before invading England, Harald Hardrada of Norway served as a mercenary in this military order.
question.text: Name this elite army unit that served as the personal bodyguards to the emperors of the Byzantine Empire.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.text: This general helped put down the Nika Riots with Mundus and Narses. This general led the campaigns against the Vandals and the Goths under Justinian the Great.
swap.clue: This general's campaigns informed Procopius's History of the Wars.

question.text: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.
question.clue: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.

swap.text: Convened by Marcian, it overturned the decision of the "synod of robbers" at Ephesus two years earlier with regard to the teachings of Eutyches. For 15 points, identify this 451 CE ecumenical council, which approved Pope Leo I's Tome, thus rejecting the Monophysite heresy.
swap.clue: Pope Leo I rejected Canon Twenty-Eight since it ran contradictory to previous canons from Nicaea.

question.leadin: His Corpus Juris Civilis codified Roman law, and his numerous building projects included the Hagia Sofia.
question.text: Name this husband of Theodora, a Byzantine emperor whose rule was chronicled by Procopius.
question.answerHtml: Justinian I the Great [or Flavius Petrus Sabbatius or Favius Anicius Justinianus Magnus]

swap.text: One exception to the rule about unblemished features was the second Byzantine ruler of this name, who took the throne after exile despite having his nose cut off. Another Byzantine ruler of this name put down the Nika Revolt.
swap.clue: Before his first overthrow, he lost the Battle of Sebastopolis to the Umayyads, after which this ruler ordered the butchering of all the Slavs in Bithynia.

question.text: The crowning Seljuk military achievement was this 1071 victory over the forces of Romanos IV, at which half the Byzantine army didn't show up to fight and the Turks harassed the rest to death.
question.clue: The victorious commander arranged his troops in a crescent formation with his archers at the rear, which enabled him to constantly apply pressure on the right and left flanks of his enemy.

swap.leadin: Name some things about Christian Heresies before the Protestant Reformation.
swap.text: One heresy relies on the literal translation of the Ten Commandments,which forbids worshipping these "graven images." In the 8th century, the Eastern Church and Leo III banned the use of these images which often depict Jesus, Saints, and Angels.

question.text: After the Battle of Adrianople, the Bulgar tsar Kaloyan made a cup from the skull of the first Latin Emperor, who had this name. The final ruler of the Latin Empire, who sold the Crown of Thorns to Louis IX, also had this name.
question.answerHtml: Baldwin [or Baudouin; or Baldwin I; or Baldwin II; or Baldwin of Courtenay]
question.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

swap.leadin: Name some people whose writings serve as important primary sources about the Byzantine Empire.
swap.text: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.
swap.clue: This woman wrote admiringly of the manly traits of Empress Irene in her influential Byzantine history, The Alexiad.

question.leadin: This ruler recognized Stefan Nemanja ("NEH-mahn-yah") as the rightful zupan ("zhoo-pan") during an incredibly successful campaign through Serbia.
question.text: Identify this expansionist Byzantine emperor whose reign was chronicled by his loyal historian John Cinnamus. He magnanimously forgave Raynald of Chatillon ("shah-tee-YON") for his Cyprian massacre in exchange for total fealty.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers were orchestrated in part by this Byzantine Emperor, who retook Constantinople from the Latin Empire and founded a namesake dynasty that ruled until 1453.
swap.answerHtml: Michael VIII Palaiologos [accept either of the second two underlined portions along with the first one; prompt on “Michael”]
swap.clue: This figure's diplomatic acumen and willingness to bankrupt his treasury helped Pedro III of Aragon, overthrowing Charles of Anjou in the Sicilian Vespers.

question.text: This archbishop of Thessalonica is known for his eyewitness account of the city's sack by and the Odyssey . Norman forces in 1185 and for a set of commentaries on the Iliad

swap.text: A Pecheneg siege of Constantinople in 1090 was defeated by this Byzantine emperor and his Cuman allies. His daughter Anna Comnenus wrote a biography of him, and he ruled during the First Crusade.
swap.clue: This ruler lost the Battle of Dyrrhachium to Robert Guiscard during a Norman invasion of his territory; Guiscard's death is related in Book 6 of a historical text compiled by this man's daughter, Anna, and named for him.
